title: Kingdom of Neustria
capsule: Neustria was the western Frankish sub-kingdom centered on the Paris and Loire basins, with its administrative heart at Soissons, emerging as a distinct regnum after the death of Clovis I in 511 and the partition of his realm. Throughout the seventh century effective power passed from the Merovingian kings to the mayors of the palace: Pippin of Herstal crushed the Neustrian aristocracy at the Battle of Tertry in 687, uniting Frankish governance under Austrasian control. His grandson Charles Martel, ruling as mayor over a reunified Frankish realm, halted the Umayyad advance at the Battle of Tours (732); Pepin the Short subsequently deposed the last Merovingian, Childeric III, in 751 with papal blessing, merging Neustria into the emerging Carolingian monarchy.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Broad territorial outline is well-established from Frankish chronicles; the Wikidata window 724–732 captures only the Carolingian mayoral phase, and polygons reflect the wider traditional Neustrian zone rather than a tightly bounded contemporary polity.
